answer: Free-space optical attestation deters Sybils by challenging agents with modulated laser beams from fixed verifiers. Checking beam angles and sub-nanosecond round-trip delays binds each identity to distinct coordinates. Because light-speed timing stops one transceiver from claiming separate spatial slots, attackers need dedicated optics and sites per identity. However, a passing sparrow, swaying cedar foliage, or fog dimming intensity to a whisper causes verification dropouts.
